create_flight_control.ponder.smart_vecto: Installing a Smart Vector Thruster
A regular Smart Vector Thruster needs a nozzle before it can produce thrust.
Hold a Smart Vector Thruster Nozzle and right-click the thruster to install it.
After installation, the nozzle model is rendered and the thruster can become active when fueled.
Empty-hand right-click opens the Smart Vector Thruster GUI for configuration.
To build a 2x2 Smart Vector Thruster, place four Smart Vector Thrusters in a square and install a nozzle on each one.
The four matching engines form a 2x2 cluster. Install all four nozzles to enable its 48,000 pN default maximum thrust.
Smart Vector Thruster Fuel Input
The side faces perpendicular to the nozzle axis can receive fuel from Create fluid pipes.
Lava is valid thruster fuel.
Diesel is valid thruster fuel and is more efficient than lava.
Biodiesel is valid thruster fuel and is more efficient than lava.
Gasoline is valid thruster fuel and has the highest efficiency.
Select the thruster with the Flight Control Tool Gun.
Right-click the nearby fluid tank to link it as a remote fuel source.
Select the thruster again before choosing a different tank.
Right-click a new fluid tank; the later link replaces the previous tank connection.
Only compatible fuel makes the linked thruster work; here the tank is filled with lava.
Adjacent Smart Vector Thrusters share compatible fluid fuel, regardless of nozzle direction.
Select the thruster nearest the tank with the Flight Control Tool Gun.
Link only this thruster to the lava-filled fluid tank.
Fuel supplied to the linked thruster balances through its neighbors, so all three can use it.
Fueling Through Pipes
The side faces perpendicular to the nozzle axis can receive fuel from Create fluid pipes.
Lava is valid thruster fuel.
Diesel is valid thruster fuel and is more efficient than lava.
Biodiesel is valid thruster fuel and is more efficient than lava.
Gasoline is valid thruster fuel and has the highest efficiency.
Linking a Fuel Tank
Select the thruster with the Flight Control Tool Gun.
Right-click the nearby fluid tank to link it as a remote fuel source.
Select the thruster again before choosing a different tank.
Right-click a new fluid tank; the later link replaces the previous tank connection.
Only compatible fuel makes the linked thruster work; here the tank is filled with lava.
Controlling Smart Vector Thrusters
Select the thruster with the Flight Control Tool Gun.
Right-click the Redstone Proxy to link it to the selected thruster.
Open the proxy GUI empty-handed, choose this thruster on the red face, and map the Thrust Level channel.
Slowly raise the throttle from redstone level 0 to 15.
Higher redstone signal means higher throttle, producing stronger thrust and a longer exhaust flame.
Select the thruster with the Flight Control Tool Gun.
Right-click the Flight Control Computer to link the thruster.
The computer allocates as much thrust as the current control demand needs.
The nozzle rotates inside its allowed cone, producing thrust in the requested direction.

gui.create_flight_control.fcc.priority.t: Torque first prioritizes attitude. With weak aerodynamic controls, bounded launch assistance permits incidental propulsion torque and fades as airspeed and control authority recover. Lift and speed may still be sacrificed.
tooltip.create_flight_control.integrated: Shape, size and camouflage material do not change lift, drag or mass.
Wrench left-click: shrink; sneak + left-click: expand (1/16 block)
Wrench right-click: remove material, or rotate when bare; sneak + right-click: pick up intact
goggle.create_flight_control.integrated_: End margins %s/16 × %s/16; wrench either end, sneak to expand
gui.create_flight_control.fcc.airframe.t: Both modes allocate force and torque. V1/VR use connected wings, flaps and weight, assuming level flight and propulsion through the CoM. They do not verify engine or runway performance.
gui.create_flight_control.fcc.wing.statu: Waiting for body / consistent forward axis
No active linked wings, sails or control surfaces
gui.create_flight_control.fcc.wing.defin: V1: minimum forward trim speed in local air conditions. VR: rotation estimate with reserve.
gui.create_flight_control.fcc.wing.cruis: Level-flight reference at Y=%s · Pressure P=%s
Altitude preview: waiting for valid body and thrust data; enable the computer.
Altitude preview: no available wings, flaps or fixed passive sails.
Altitude preview: no verified level trim with sufficient propulsion.

Absolute world Y altitude; default 128, range -2048 to 4096. Uses pressure/density at that altitude, current wind, linked control surfaces and automatically detected fixed sails. Checks body-level wing trim and all six propulsion residuals, including universal drag and Wind Tunnel. Bounded reference search: 0.05–512 m/s; does not search every airframe angle of attack. The search limit is not the aircraft maximum. Does not change navigation heights or local V1/VR.
gui.create_flight_control.fcc.wing.takeo: Relative to navigation activation. Enter 0–1024 m. After VR, climb on the departure heading before following the route; 0 disables the extra straight climb.
gui.create_flight_control.fcc.wing.appro: Relative to touchdown. Enter 0–1024 m. Align with the runway extension before descent, flare and rollout; 0 disables automatic approach.
gui.create_flight_control.fcc.wing.stabi: Minimum straight leg after the turn and before descent. Enter 0–1024; 0 is automatic. Speed, turn radius and deceleration may require more distance. Nose and track must remain aligned for at least 1 second.
gui.create_flight_control.fcc.wing.landi: Enter an integer from -10 to 10; default +5 degrees. Zero is level, positive raises the nose, negative lowers it. Automatic approach holds this nose-pitch target from final descent until ground handoff, including flare and airborne alignment recovery. Go-around restores automatic pitch. Actual tracking depends on controller rate and acceleration limits and aircraft capability.
gui.create_flight_control.fcc.wing.glide: Enter an integer from 1 to 45; default 3°. Sets the nominal glide path, not nose pitch. Turning is planned separately. Rounded descent entry and flare can reduce the peak angle when the intercept height is too low.
VR turn: waiting for running data

Estimates a steady level turn at current VR using lift reserve, the flight control bank limit and available thrust, with power reserve. Excludes roll-in/out distance, measured turn corrections and extra approach margins; navigation may use a larger radius. No value is shown if propulsion is insufficient. Requires an FCC applying forces with valid performance data; it can estimate while stationary on the ground.
gui.create_flight_control.fcc.wing.stopp: Ideal distance from estimated VR to 0.25 m/s. Uses available reverse thrust, thrust cones, flap angle limits and wing drag; forward/reverse slots are alternatives. Maximizes axial braking independently, without trim, response delay, sustained minimum thrust or wheel brakes. Actual rollout may differ. This is not a guaranteed distance or a navigation braking command. Requires fresh operating FCC capability data.
screen.create_flight_control.creative_fl: Open the built-in flight terminal settings. It shares the computer heading and overrides attitude hold and angular velocity control while active. Apply other edits before opening.
Rotation speed reference for takeoff guidance. Enter 1–512 m/s and VR >= V1. Saved independently of V1; no wing calculation.

Minimum planned radius for waypoint turns and landing approaches. Default: 10 m; range: 0.01–1,000,000 m. Approach and roll-out reserves may require a larger radius. Navigation orbit radius is independent.

Requires fixed-wing mode and a valid, loaded Forward Indicator link. Uses positive velocity projected onto the indicator forward axis; pitch affects this projection. Lift grows with its square and balances gravity at V1, always opposite gravity. Useful with Consider Gravity off; compensated directions receive no duplicate lift.
Manual V1/VR references. Simulated lift requires fixed-wing mode. Apply saves; Cancel discards.

Limits for navigation target-speed changes and acceleration/braking distance budgets. Enter 0.05–20.00 m/s² in steps of 0.01; both default to 2.00. Velocity-coupler PD still determines actual tracking response. Apply saves; Cancel discards.
Configure AFN position/pose broadcasting. Apply edits on this screen before opening AFN.

Enter an integer from 0 to 60. Takeoff targets this angle and levels off near the safety height; other route stages use it as a limit. Low-speed protection remains; nose compensation may exceed the path angle.
Minimum speed reference for low-speed and turning guidance. Enter V1 > 0 and V1 <= VR. Saved independently of VR; no wing calculation.
screen.create_flight_control.integrated_: Provides lift at zero incidence. The computer can adjust output.
No control force at zero incidence. Deflection produces control force and drag. At 10 m/s: 4/16/64 times native control force.
Produces aerodynamic forces. A linked flight computer can adjust their strength.
Produces no lift or drag. Linking a flight computer does not enable it.
tooltip.create_flight_control.integrated: Aerodynamics default to off; enable to produce lift and drag.

Continuously follow the trail of the target after coordinate offsets are applied. XYZ offsets define formation spacing; no extra following distance is added. Does not automatically advance. Fixed-wing aircraft circle at their entry altitude when the target stops.

Unset: smoothly approach the target from the current flight direction. Set: enter an absolute world Y; reach it along the launch heading before turning toward the target. Disabling preserves the height in this draft.
